newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian oil workers partly shut down piplelines.
newsitem.headline: Colombian oil workers partly shut down piplelines.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 7 Reuter - Colombia's main oil workers' union said Monday that it had begun temporarily halting pumping operations along piplelines belonging to the state oil company Ecopetrol to protest government privatization plans.

A statement from the 7,000-strong union, known by its acronym USO, said the action began at midnight Sunday and added that pumping operations were being shut down every four hours for what it described as "escalating" time periods.

Ecopetrol officials said there had been no immediate effect on Colombia's oil output, but USO said the action had affected pumping from fields in northeastern Arauca province, Casanare in the eastern plains and Huila in the southwest.
The statement also said the action had adversely affected the dispatch of oil and fuel products from Colombia's refineries in Barrancabermeja, Cartagena, Orito and Apray.

USO, which is currently negotiating a new collective contract with Ecopetrol, is calling for a 30 percent pay hike for its members and an end to what it claims are plans for the creeping privatization of Ecopetrol.
The union, known for its fiercely nationalistic stance, said Monday's action was prompted, at least in part, by plans to privatize all pipleline operations.

It also said it was protesting against plans to provide more favorable contract terms to British Petroleum Co Plc for the exploitation of the Piedemonte block in the eastern plains and what it described as Ecopetrol's plans to privatize the natural gas transporation business in Colombia.
